sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 933.

PD 933.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 933 was established by Ordinance No. 29586, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 10, 2014. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 933 is established on property generally bounded by Singleton Boulevard, Obenchain Street, Duluth Street, and Borger Street. The size of PD 933 is approximately 24.782 acres. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Creation Of Subareas
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.103. CREATION OF SUBAREAS.

This district is divided into five subareas: Subarea A, Subarea B, Subarea C, Subarea D, and Subarea E. The boundaries of each subarea are shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit 933A). (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. In this district:

(1) BLADE SIGN means a sign projecting perpendicularly from a main building facade, visible from both sides, and made of rigid or soft fabric materials.

(2) MAJOR RETAIL USE means a single-occupant retail or personal service use with a floor area greater than 30,000 square feet and equal to or less than 85,000 square feet.

(3) OPEN SPACE means an area that is principally open to the sky but allows for architectural elements such as colonnades, pergolas, and gazebos and may include paved areas.

(4) SMALL SHRUB means a shrub that typically reaches a height of 18 to 30 inches upon maturity, but may exceed 30 inches in height.

(5) STOOP means a small porch that leads to the entrance of a residence.

(c) Subareas A and B are considered to be residential zoning districts.

(d) Subareas C, D, and E are considered to be nonresidential zoning districts. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.105. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 933A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 933B: Subarea A development plan.

(3) Exhibit 933C: equivalency table. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 933A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district.

(2) Development plans may be submitted in phases and may include any portion of the Property.

(3) If there is a conflict between the text of this article and a development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Subarea A. Development and use of the Property must comply with the Subarea A development plan (Exhibit 933B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(c) Single family and handicapped group dwelling unit. For single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, a preliminary plat approved by the city plan commission satisfies the development plan requirement in this section. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-2 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-2 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-2 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-2 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main uses are permitted:

-- Alcoholic beverage establishment.

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(b)(3) is not met.] -- Single family.

(c) In Subarea A, the following uses are the only main uses permitted:

-- Duplex. -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(b)(3) is not met.] -- Multifamily. -- Retirement housing. -- Single family.

(d) In Subarea B, the following uses are the only main uses permitted:

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(b)(3) is not met.] -- Single family.

(e) The following uses are not permitted:

-- Attached non-premise sign. -- General merchandise or food store 100,000 square feet or more. -- Mini-warehouse.

(f) For lodging uses, rooms may only be accessed through an internal corridor. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.109. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-2 Mixed Use District apply.

(2) In this district, additional yard, lot, or space regulations triggered by adjacency to a single family or handicapped group dwelling unit use do not apply.

(b) Front yard.

(1) Subareas A, C, and E.

(A) In general.

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, minimum front yard is not required.

(ii) Urban form setback is not required.

(iii) Except as provided in this subparagraph, maximum front yard is 20 feet. A portion of the front facade equal to at least 70 percent of the length of the lot, excluding pedestrian and vehicular ingress and egress points, must be located within the maximum front yard setback.

(B) Single family and handicapped group dwelling unit structures.

(i) Minimum front yard is nine feet.

(ii) Maximum front yard is not required.

(2) Subarea D.

(A) Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(B) Maximum front yard is not required.

(3) Encroachments.

(A) Balconies, awnings, cantilevered roof eaves, and other architectural features may encroach into a required front yard and above paved areas intended for pedestrian or vehicular movement if:

(i) a minimum of nine feet of clearance above grade is provided for single family and handicapped group dwelling unit structures; and

(ii) a minimum of 10 feet of clearance above grade is provided for all other structures.

(B) Stoops and steps may encroach up to six feet into a required front yard.

(c) Side and rear yard. Minimum side or rear yard is not required. Tower spacing is not required.

(d) Density. Maximum total number of dwelling units is 1,500 with no maximum number of dwelling units per acre, except that for Subarea B, maximum number of dwelling units is 130.

(e) Floor area.

(1) Residential uses. No maximum floor area.

(2) Nonresidential uses. Except as provided in this subsection, maximum floor area is 2,159,000 square feet.

(A) For alcoholic beverage establishments, maximum total floor area for all uses is 15,000 square feet, with a maximum floor area of 5,000 square feet for any single alcoholic beverage establishment use.

(B) One major retail use is permitted.

(C) A single-occupant retail or personal service use may not exceed 85,000 square feet in floor area.

(f) Equivalencies. The maximum density and floor area in Subsections (d) and (e) may be adjusted using the equivalency table (Exhibit 933C).

(g) Height.

(1) In general. Except as provided on the conceptual plan, maximum structure height is 90 feet.

(2) Projections. The following structures may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height:

(A) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead or stair bulkhead.

(B) Mechanical equipment room.

(C) Cooling tower.

(D) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(E) Ornamental cupola or dome.

(F) Skylights.

(G) Clerestory.

(H) Visual screens which surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(I) Chimney and vent stacks.

(J) Amateur communications tower.

(K) Parapet wall limited to a height of four feet.

(h) Lot size. For single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, minimum lot size is 1,000 square feet. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses.

(1) A minimum of 0.25 visitor parking spaces per dwelling unit is required.

(2) A shared access development is considered to be one lot for purposes of this subsection.

(c) Location of surface parking.

(1) Except single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, in Subareas A, C, and E, surface parking may not be located between a building and a street.

(2) In Subarea D, surface parking may not be located between a building and Singleton Boulevard. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: On-Street Parking Reduction
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.112. ON-STREET PARKING REDUCTION.

(a) Except as provided in this section, any on-street parking spaces may be counted as a reduction of the parking requirement for a multifamily use adjacent to the on-street parking space or the visitor parking requirement for a single family or handicapped group dwelling unit use adjacent to the on- street parking space.

(b) An on-street parking space may not be used to reduce the required parking for more than one use.

(c) For multifamily uses, on-street parking spaces may be counted as a maximum parking reduction of 2.5 percent.

(d) An on-street parking space that is not available to the public at all times of the day may only be counted as a partial parking space in proportion to the amount of time that it is available. For example, a parking space that is available to the public only eight hours per day will be counted as one- third of a parking space (8  24 = one-third). The total of the limited-availability parking spaces will be counted to the nearest whole number, with one-half counted as an additional space. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.113. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Urban Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.114. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Applicability.

(1) Regulations governing building facades and materials apply to any building constructed after December 10, 2014.

(2) Regulations governing screening, pedestrian amenities, and pedestrian lighting apply to buildings constructed after December 10, 2014 and to buildings completed before December 10, 2014 if a building permit is issued to add more than 5,000 square feet in floor area to the building.

(b) Street-facing facades.

(1) For each street-level office or retail use, the facade must have clear glazing that covers a minimum of:

(A) 70 percent of the street-level facade for a retail use; or

(B) 40 percent of the street-level facade for an office use.

(2) For multifamily and nonresidential uses, street-facing facades must have a minimum of three of the following building elements: raised parapet, canopies, deep-set windows, varied roof forms designed to create visual interest, pilasters, cornices, string courses, window sills, awnings, lintels, or rustication. Except for awnings, building elements must be constructed of brick, cast stone, stone, ornamental metal, concrete, cellular PVC, cementitious panels or trim, or cement plaster stucco.

(3) No more than one service entrance for every 300 feet of street frontage may be located on Singleton Boulevard.

(4) Continuous street-facing facades must step back a minimum depth of two feet for a minimum distance of 10 feet for every 75 feet of length. Balconies, wall headers, canopies, awnings, cornices, window sills, and roof eaves are allowed to project into required facade step backs.

(c) Building materials.

(1) For street-level office or retail uses, only clear glass windows are allowed.

(2) For multifamily and nonresidential uses, the following building materials may not exceed 25 percent of the total area of a building facade:

(A) wood;

(B) corrugated sheet metal; and

(C) galvanized metal.

(3) In addition to glass, the exterior cladding must have at least two other facade materials on each street-facing facade.

(d) Entrances.

(1) Primary entrances to a building may not be located off of surface parking lots.

(2) Except as provided in this subsection, awnings, canopies, attached towers, or turrets must be provided over pedestrian building entrances.

(3) Single family, handicapped group dwelling unit, and multifamily uses may use stairs, stoops, and unenclosed porches at pedestrian building entrances.

(4) For residential uses with street-level access, at least 65 percent of individual dwelling unit entries must provide direct access via an improved pedestrian way to the sidewalk along abutting streets and abutting, privately owned, publicly accessible driveways. A dwelling unit is not required to have more than one point of access. The Property is considered one lot for purposes of complying with the requirements of this paragraph.

(5) For separate retail uses with street-level frontage on Singleton Boulevard, individual entryways must be provided for each use with the main entrances on Singleton Boulevard.

(e) Screening.

(1) Trash, storage, and loading areas must be screened as follows:

(A) by fencing or opaque plantings at least six feet in height at maturity; or

(B) be located inside the building, away from the street edge, and behind a facade treated architecturally in a manner similar to the building.

(2) Service areas must be enclosed by gates a minimum of six feet in height.

(3) Service elements on roofs must be screened so that they are not visible from any public right-of-way.

(f) Pedestrian amenities. Along Singleton Boulevard, a minimum of one bench, one trash receptacle, and one five-bicycle parking rack must be provided for every 300 feet of street frontage, with any fraction of frontage rounding up. For example, a street frontage with 350 feet would require a minimum of two of each of the pedestrian amenities.

(g) Pedestrian lighting.

(1) Lights must be pedestrian-scaled with a maximum height of 16 feet to the top of the fixture.

(2) Lights must be located within a public right-of-way or public access easement or as near thereto as practicable to illuminate sidewalks.

(3) Light standards must be spaced between 60 feet and 120 feet apart, alternate with tree spacing, and with the center of the foundation of the light standard approximately two feet from back of the curb. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.115. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Shared access development.

(1) Landscape area. A minimum of 10 percent of the shared access development must be designated as landscape area. Permeable pavement may not be counted as landscape area.

(2) Site trees. One tree with a caliper equal to or exceeding two inches must be provided for each individual lot. The tree may be located on the individual lot, in the front yard, or in the parkway with a license approved by city council. A street tree may count as a required site tree.

(3) Street trees.

(A) One large tree having a caliper of at least three inches must be provided for every 60 feet of street frontage.

(B) Street trees must be spaced a minimum of 20 feet apart, with spacing no greater than 60 feet apart, excluding driveways and visibility triangles.

(C) Street trees must have an eight foot clearance over the sidewalk.

(D) The building official may approve alternate locations for street trees within 30 feet of the Property line if utility obstructions prevent planting within the required area.

(c) Other uses.

(1) Perimeter landscape buffer strip.

(A) A landscape buffer strip must be provided along the entire length of that portion of the perimeter of the Property with a residential adjacency, excluding driveways, access ways, and at points of ingress and egress. The landscape buffer strip must be at least 10 feet wide, except that a minimum width of eight feet is allowed for horizontal distances less than 100 feet.

(B) The landscape buffer strip may have pedestrian and other amenities such as sidewalks, retaining walls, stoops, patios, and patio fences but may not exceed 60 percent impervious surface area.

(C) The landscape buffer strip may have privately fenced patios and yards.

(D) A landscape buffer strip must have one of the following groups of plant material at an average of one group for each 50 linear feet of landscape buffer strip:

(i) One large canopy tree and one large non-canopy tree.

(ii) One large canopy tree and three small trees.

(iii) One large canopy tree and three large evergreen shrubs.

(iv) One large canopy tree, two small trees, and one large evergreen shrub.

(v) One large canopy tree, one small tree, and two large evergreen shrubs.

(vi) Two large non-canopy trees.

(vii) Two small trees and one large evergreen shrub.

(viii) Three small evergreen shrubs.

(ix) One large evergreen shrub and three small shrubs.

(2) Site trees. One site tree with a caliper equal to or exceeding two inches must be provided for every 4,000 square feet of lot area. Street trees may be counted toward the required site trees.

(3) Street trees.

(A) One large tree having a caliper of at least three inches must be provided for each 60 feet of street frontage.

(B) Street trees must be spaced a minimum of 20 feet apart, with spacing no greater than 60 feet, excluding driveways and visibility triangles.

(C) Street trees must have an eight-foot-high clearance over the sidewalk.

(d) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.116. SIDEWALKS.

(a) Sidewalks must be provided along all street-facing facades and be buffered from a street by a minimum four-foot-wide planting strip.

(b) Except as provided in this section, sidewalks must have a minimum unobstructed width of five feet.

(d) Along Singleton Boulevard, sidewalks must have a minimum unobstructed width of six feet.

(e) ADA-approved tree grates are not considered an obstruction.

(f) The building official may approve minor deviations in the width or location of required sidewalks as necessary to accommodate grade, utility locations, or similar site constraints. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Open Space
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.117. OPEN SPACE.

(a) A minimum of 43,560 square feet of open space is required.

(b) A minimum of 75 percent of the required open space must be accessible to tenants or residents of the Property.

(c) Open space may be provided in phases as shown on an approved development plan or plat. Before issuing a final certificate of occupancy or conducting a final inspection within a subarea, a minimum amount of open space must be provided as follows:

(1) One subarea developed: 8,700 square feet.

(2) Two subareas developed: 17,400 square feet.

(3) Three subareas developed: 26,100 square feet.

(4) Four subareas developed: 34,800 square feet.

(5) Five subareas developed: 43,560 square feet. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.118. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For retail uses, a minimum of two types of street-level signs are required for each 600 feet of frontage along Singleton Boulevard. Street-level signs include awning signs, projecting signs, window signs, or blade signs.

(c) Rooftop and flashing motion signs are prohibited.

(d) For temporary signs for single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, the Property is considered one lot.

(e) Projecting attached signs must provide a minimum of eight feet of clearance above grade. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Ingress And Egress
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.119. INGRESS AND EGRESS.

Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan. The final location of the driveways and drive approaches may vary from the location shown with no increase in number of drive approaches. Final design and location must be shown on an approved development plan. For a shared access development, the location of ingress and egress points must be shown on the plat. Ingress and egress for individual dwelling units or single family lots need not be shown on the plat. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Shared Access Development
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.120. SHARED ACCESS DEVELOPMENT.

(a) A maximum of 130 lots with at least four shared access points are permitted within a shared access development.

(b) Access points may provide vehicular access to a private driveway within the district if at least one shared access point provides vehicular access to a public or private street.

(c) Adjacent shared access developments may have connected shared access areas and utilities. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.121. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29586)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-933.122. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29586)
